title: A clock you can control
description:
Code that reads the time is hard to test. Write a `FakeClock` and a function that takes a clock as a parameter:

- `FakeClock(start=0.0)` has `now()` returning the current fake time and `advance(seconds)` moving it forward (a negative amount raises `ValueError`).
- `is_expired(session, clock)` returns `True` when `clock.now()` is at least `session["started"] + session["timeout"]`.

Any object with a `now()` method works as a clock, so the real program can pass one built on `time.time`.
hints: Keep the time in an attribute; `now` returns it and `advance` adds to it after checking the amount.
`is_expired` only ever calls `clock.now()`, which is what lets a test pass a fake and the program pass a real clock.
